audits.title: Clinical audit of prescribing for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and young people services (CYPS)
audits.standard: TEWV ADHD prescribing guidelines and NICE NG87 (2018)
audits.setting: Four Teesside child and adolescent community teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Verbal information given in 92% and written in 58%; pre-treatment assessment completed in all but 3; methylphenidate not first line in 4 cases; lisdexamfetamine used second line in 75%.

audits.other_findings: Of the 4 not started on methylphenidate, 3 received atomoxetine by parental choice and 1 had contraindications. Recommended updated NICE-compliant trust guidance and a trust-wide audit.
audits.citation: Parker M, Martin E. Clinical audit of prescribing for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and young people services (CYPS). BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S45-S45. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.170.

audits.title: Monitoring of ADHD Medication: Are We in Line With NICE Guidelines? a Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE: weight, blood pressure and heart rate monitored every 6 months on ADHD medication
audits.setting: Community mental health team, Glasgow, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde

cycle1.result: Weight recorded 15%, heart rate 8%, blood pressure 19%.

audits.intervention: Results presented at a local meeting with relevant clinicians in May 2021

cycle2.result: Weight recorded 45%, heart rate 40%, blood pressure 50%.

audits.other_findings: 30 patients identified, 10 excluded for non-engagement. Still not meeting NICE guidance; COVID-19 reduced face-to-face reviews.
audits.citation: Langan C. Monitoring of ADHD Medication: Are We in Line With NICE Guidelines? a Closed Loop Audit. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S163-S163. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.459.

audits.title: Physical Health Assessment and Monitoring for Adults Receiving Pharmacological Treatment for ADHD in an Adult CMHT:Clinical Audit
audits.standard: NICE: baseline height, weight, pulse, blood pressure and cardiovascular assessment before stimulant treatment, then 6-monthly weight, blood pressure and pulse

cycle1.result: Baseline blood pressure 57% (19); pulse 39% (13); weight 51% (17); cardiovascular assessment 6% (2). At 6-month follow-up (10 patients), 0% had blood pressure, pulse or weight documented.

audits.intervention: New proforma for baseline and 6-monthly physical health monitoring to be placed in case notes; results presented at CMHT meeting.
audits.citation: Shankar N, Turner C, Klenka L. Physical Health Assessment and Monitoring for Adults Receiving Pharmacological Treatment for ADHD in an Adult CMHT:Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S158-S159. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.423.

audits.title: Audit of Shared Care Guideline Compliance for ADHD Patients: Monitoring Physical Observations by General Practitioners
audits.standard: NICE and shared care guidelines: blood pressure, pulse and weight monitored by the GP at least twice a year (every 6 months)
audits.setting: GP monitoring under ADHD shared care, patients due annual structured review with a specialist ADHD team

cycle1.period: Patients due review August and September 2023
cycle1.result: Blood pressure within 6 months 22/22 (100%), within 1 year 19/22 (86%); pulse 20/22 (90%) and 18/22 (81%); weight 21/22 (95%) and 20/22 (90%).

audits.intervention: Letter sent to GP practices commending the result and recommending flagging a review for weight loss of 10% or more within 12 months.
audits.other_findings: 8 of 22 had a significant blood pressure change as defined by NICE (increase of 2-4 mmHg).
audits.citation: Utomi C. Audit of Shared Care Guideline Compliance for ADHD Patients: Monitoring Physical Observations by General Practitioners. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S267-S268. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.642.

audits.title: Clinical Re-Audit of Baseline Assessment, Consideration of Medication, Titration, and Monitoring of Service Users With a Working Diagnosis of ADHD (Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder) in South Durham Tier 3 CAMHS.
audits.standard: National guidelines on ADHD medication initiation, physical health monitoring, follow-up and rating scales

cycle1.result: Pre-medication assessment 100%; regular follow-up 5/7; height and weight plotted 6/7; rating scales returned by parents 0 and schools 3/7

audits.intervention: Recommendations from previous audit, including a centralised list of service users and retrieval of rating scales

cycle2.result: Pre-medication assessment 100%; regular follow-up 5/7; physical health check within 3 months 100%; height and weight plotted 6/7; rating scales completed by parents and school 6/7; green compliance

audits.other_findings: Waiting time to start medication increased because of staffing issues.

audits.standard: NICE guidance on ADHD medication monitoring in the past 6 months
audits.setting: Mental Health of Learning Disabilities team, Kent and Medway

cycle1.result: Weight measured in last 6 months 83%; pulse 76.5%; blood pressure 64%.

audits.title: Monitoring Prescribing for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in Child & Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS): A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: NICE: height, weight, blood pressure, heart rate with centiles and growth charts for children on ADHD medication

cycle1.result: Height and weight 97%; BP and HR 100%; height/weight centiles and growth charts 85%; BP centiles 10%; HR centiles 0%.

audits.intervention: Results presented at local department meeting and posters of NICE guidelines distributed

cycle2.result: Height, weight, their centiles, HR, BP and growth charts 100%; BP centiles 2%; HR centiles 0%.

audits.other_findings: The electronic record cannot convert BP and HR to centiles, limiting compliance.

audits.title: ADHD Treatment in a Community Mental Health Team: Report of a Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: NICE standards for clinical review and physical health monitoring of ADHD drug treatment
audits.setting: Adult community mental health team, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 17.2% waiting for initiation and 12.7% in initiation phase; annual blood pressure monitoring 62.0%, annual weight 56.7%; longest wait for initiation 330 days; median initiation phase 92 days.

audits.intervention: Staff resources reallocated to create a dedicated ADHD clinic with a new process for initiation and shared-care monitoring.

cycle2.result: Keyworker allocated 99.7%, diagnosis recorded 99.1%; 12.5% waiting and 20.8% in initiation phase; annual blood pressure 90.4%, annual weight 80.3%; longest wait 125 days; median initiation phase 62 days.

audits.other_findings: Reviews offered to over 90% of monitored patients but not all; 6-monthly monitoring improved less than 12-monthly. Shared-care requests accepted by GPs increased substantially. Data also collected at 3 months.
audits.citation: Cornwall P, Rumiantsev N, Pearson A, Sutcliffe M. ADHD Treatment in a Community Mental Health Team: Report of a Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S145-S145. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11363.

audits.title: An Audit on the Prevalence of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in the General Adult Community Mental Health Team Caseload and Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines on Physical Health monitoring
audits.standard: NICE ADHD guidelines: baseline observations, 6-monthly weight, HR and BP, 6-monthly psychiatry review, side-effect assessment
audits.setting: General adult community mental health team, Southern Trust

cycle1.result: 9/21 (43%) lacked baseline observations; 14/21 (67%) no 6-monthly weight; 15/21 (71%) no 6-monthly HR/BP; 8/21 (38%) no 6-month psychiatry review; 1/21 (5%) letters no side-effect discussion; 10/21 not under PHMT or a key worker.

audits.intervention: Identifiable ADHD caseload created; patients referred to the Physical Health Monitoring Team; reflection on more specific side-effect documentation.
audits.other_findings: 21/31 patients with confirmed ADHD were medicated; side-effect documentation varied (48% general, 38% specific).
audits.citation: McKaigue H, McNamara R. An Audit on the Prevalence of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in the General Adult Community Mental Health Team Caseload and Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines on Physical Health monitoring. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S318-S318. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11667.

audits.title: An Audit of Practice Quality and Alignment With Evidence Based Standards
audits.standard: NICE: blood pressure, heart rate and weight before starting ADHD medication and at least six-monthly, with structured side-effect reviews
audits.setting: YCC community mental health team, adult ADHD patients (Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board)

cycle1.result: Physical health observations recorded for 174 (84.1%), often incomplete; monitoring within NICE intervals in 30.9%, 6–12 months in 28.5%, beyond 12 months in 24.6% and no monitoring in 15.9%.

audits.other_findings: No standardised monitoring tool was used; barriers included limited access to monitoring equipment and continued prescribing despite non-attendance. Electronic prompts and standardised monitoring templates were recommended.
audits.citation: Elsout M, Ahmed A, Beggan K, Evans R, Kota S. An Audit of Practice Quality and Alignment With Evidence Based Standards. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S290-S291. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11725.
